landing.faq.description: Everything you need to know before getting started.
landing.faq.stack.question: What's the tech stack?
landing.faq.stack.answer: Next.js 16 with the App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict mode, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Drizzle ORM, and better-auth. Every piece of business logic is inlined — no external packages for payment, email, storage, or AI.
landing.faq.payment.question: Which payment providers are supported?
landing.faq.payment.answer: Stripe, PayPal, Creem, Alipay, and WeChat Pay out of the box. The PaymentManager abstraction makes it straightforward to add more providers by implementing a single interface.
landing.faq.database.question: Which databases can I use?
landing.faq.database.answer: Drizzle ORM handles PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Turso, and Cloudflare D1. Switch providers by editing DATABASE_PROVIDER in your .env — the schema templates and drizzle config adapt automatically.
landing.faq.customize.question: How customizable is the landing page?
landing.faq.customize.answer: The src/blocks/ directory ships with demo sections — they're designed to be rewritten per project. The durable primitives live in src/components/, so your rebrand touches blocks and translations, not the chassis.
landing.faq.license.question: Can I use this for commercial projects?
landing.faq.license.answer: Yes. ShipAny Next is built for shipping production SaaS products. You own the code after cloning — no per-seat fees, no runtime dependencies on our infrastructure.
landing.cta.headline: Ready to ship your SaaS?
landing.cta.subheadline: Stop wiring auth, payments, and RBAC from scratch. Start with ShipAny Next and build what actually makes your product unique.

site.seo.what_description: Genjutsu is a video-to-video model by Higgsfield. You upload an existing clip; this site uses the model to restyle scenes, styles, products, and props around the same subject while preserving the original motion, camera movement, and timing. It is not a from-scratch text-to-video generator — and it is not a face-swap or identity-swap tool. The source take provides the motion; Genjutsu changes the world around it.

site.seo.change_desc: Same subject — new scene, style, product, or a single object.

site.seo.vs_title: Our Tool vs the Official Higgsfield Genjutsu
site.seo.vs_description: Same underlying model. Different way to pay. Use the official app if you want the full Higgsfield suite on a subscription; use this site if you prefer prepaid credits for Genjutsu jobs only.
site.seo.cta_description: Upload a video, write the result you want, and generate. The tool is at the top of this page.

site.seo.step2_desc: Write what should change — scene, style, product, or prop. Keep the original subject.
site.seo.step3_desc: Genjutsu restyles the world around the subject while preserving the original movement and shot timing.
site.seo.change_products_desc: Replace a featured product while preserving the original camera move, framing, and timing.
site.seo.change_styles_desc: Keep the same subject — restyle the look: anime, cinematic, vintage, or material treatments.
site.seo.change_scenes_desc: Restage the location around a locked camera move: interior to alley, day to night, studio to street.
site.seo.change_props_desc: Swap an object in frame (cup, vase, package) without rebuilding the take or changing the subject.

site.seo.faq1_a: Genjutsu is a Higgsfield video-to-video model. This site uses it to restyle scenes, styles, products, and props around the same subject while keeping the original camera movement and timing — without changing who or what is in the shot.
site.seo.faq2_q: Does Genjutsu AI support face swapping?
site.seo.faq2_a: No. Genjutsu AI does not support face swapping or identity replacement. If a reference image contains a real human face, it is rejected before generation. Anime, cartoon, illustration, and 3D characters are allowed. See our Terms of Service (/terms-of-service) for prohibited categories, detection, reporting, and enforcement.
site.seo.faq3_q: How is this different from text-to-video?
site.seo.faq3_a: You start with a real take. The model does not invent a new camera path from a prompt alone. It transfers or preserves the motion already in the file you upload.
site.seo.faq4_q: What can I change in a clip?
site.seo.faq4_a: Scenes, styles, products, and props. Aim for a full environment restage, a style filter, or a local object swap — while keeping the original subject intact.
site.seo.faq5_q: Do I need a Higgsfield subscription?
site.seo.faq5_a: No. This site sells prepaid credit packs and charges per generation. The official Higgsfield product is subscription-based if you prefer to work there instead.
site.seo.faq6_a: Each job is estimated from the provider cost for your input duration and resolution. Input length is rounded up to the next whole second. The exact credit reserve is calculated on the server before generation starts.
site.seo.faq7_q: How long does a generation take?
site.seo.faq7_a: Typical jobs finish in minutes, depending on clip length, resolution, and queue. You can leave the page and check status; the task is tracked on the server.
site.seo.faq8_a: 480p, 720p, and 1080p. Higher resolution costs more credits because the provider charges more per second of input video.
site.seo.faq9_q: Can I use the output commercially?
site.seo.faq9_a: You may use generated videos subject to our Terms of Service, Higgsfield usage rules, and applicable law. Do not upload footage you do not have rights to edit.

site.testimonials.title: What Creators Say About Genjutsu AI
site.testimonials.subtitle: Editors, producers, and short-form teams using video-to-video to keep the original motion
site.testimonials.quote1: I swapped the featured product in a tracking shot and the camera still followed the same path. Genjutsu kept the motion so the edit dropped straight into the cut.
site.testimonials.quote2: Object Swap let us restage a product in a new scene without reshooting. Original timing stayed intact — that is the whole point of video-to-video.
site.testimonials.quote3: Pay-per-generation credits beat a monthly Higgsfield seat for our volume. We run a few Genjutsu jobs a week, not every day.
site.testimonials.quote4: Wardrobe tests used to mean another studio day. Now I upload the take, prompt the look, and keep the original blocking.
site.testimonials.quote5: Minutes, not overnight renders. I restyle products, styles, and scenes, download, and post. Motion transfer keeps it feeling like the same shot.
site.testimonials.quote6: We use it for product previsualization: same camera move, different product treatment. Concept reviews got faster because the timing is already locked.
site.testimonials.quote7: Credits are transparent enough for client billing. Each job is one clip, one prompt, one charge — no unused subscription sitting in the budget.
site.testimonials.quote8: Scene swap on a locked tracking shot sold the location change. We still had to grade, but we did not have to recast or rebuild the move.
site.testimonials.quote9: I pick 720p for drafts and 1080p for finals. Paying only for seconds of input video is easier to explain than a studio plan.
